conclusions.statement: schedule-unroll-k 1->2 at the 8x8x8 tile is profitable on every shape tested
conclusions.basis: 5 independent shapes tested (8x8x8-derived small_control excluded, not a comparable pair), all classified A

conclusions.statement: the effect generalizes to matmul shapes broadly (any M/N/K, any tile)
conclusions.basis: only 5 shapes tested, all at the SAME tile (8x8x8) and SAME unroll factor (2); no data exists for other tiles/unroll factors across multiple shapes, and no data exists for non-matmul kernels

conclusions.statement: speedup magnitude varies across shapes (10.2%-31.5%) but sign (positive) is consistent
conclusions.basis: observed directly across 5 shapes, not fit from a formula

conclusions.statement: speedup magnitude correlates with K-loop trip count or code-size growth in a fittable, predictive way
conclusions.basis: only 5 data points available; a regression fit from 5 points would be a curve through noise, not a validated model -- task brief section 9 explicitly requires discrete evidence buckets over an unjustified formula at this sample size

conclusions.statement: spilling candidates can be profitable even though spills are a real backend cost
conclusions.basis: directly measured for 2 of 2 tested Group B diagnostics (full-K-unroll, alt-K-tile) -- both faster than their matched baselines despite spills

conclusions.statement: spilling candidates are USUALLY profitable / spills rarely matter in general
conclusions.basis: only 2 spilling candidates were ever measured, both from the same 32x32x32 shape and same underlying tile/unroll mechanism -- suggestive, not sufficient to generalize across problem sizes where the spilled working set no longer fits L1
